title: Prestige TV
summary: A show, a season, and a supporting character. Nobody checks the first two.

larp.dek: The canon is small and the opinions are borrowed from the same four essays. You pass until somebody names a season.

crib.heading: References
lines: The Sopranos, The Wire, Mad Men. The three-name spine.
Season two is the contested one, in almost every show.
The Wire season four is the correct answer and saying it marks you as ordinary.
Prestige is a budget and a runtime before it is a quality.

crib.heading: Opinions to hold
lines: The finale discourse is more interesting than the finales.
Six episodes is not a season.
Every show got worse once it knew it was prestige.

phrases.line: Season three is where it loses the thread.
phrases.when: Any long-running show. There is always a weak middle and this is proof of attendance.
phrases.invites: "What happens in three?" Move to why the pacing changed, not what happened.

phrases.line: I'm one episode from the end and I'm rationing it.
phrases.when: Asked whether you have finished. It explains the gap and flatters the show.

phrases.line: It's the one scene everybody talks about, and it earned it.
phrases.when: Somebody mentions the famous episode. Agreement costs nothing.

follow_up.question: "Which season?"
follow_up.why: It is the only question in the form and it gets asked constantly, because seasons are how people who actually watched store the show.

counter.move: Pick the middle season and complain about it. Every long show has a weak middle and having an opinion about it is proof of attendance in a way that praising the finale is not.
counter.holds: A long conversation. It fails against somebody who wants to talk about one specific episode, because that is a memory and not a position.

tells: You quote the famous line. Everyone has the famous line, it was in the trailer.
You talk about the writing. Viewers talk about one scene.
You have no show you gave up on. Everyone has one and it is usually season three.
cost: None worth counting. This is the lowest-stakes claim on the site.
Somebody will spoil something for you, which is the only enforcement this scene has.

hard_spoilers.reveal: The Sopranos ends on Tony in a diner, Journey on the jukebox, and a cut to ten seconds of black mid-sentence. No death is shown. Chase has never confirmed one.
hard_spoilers.lands_because: Everybody knows it cuts to black. What separates the watchers is knowing the cut lands inside the line, that the scene had spent two minutes teaching you to look up every time the door chimed, and that the argument is about editing grammar rather than about whether Tony died. That is not a secondhand detail.
hard_spoilers.where: The Sopranos, “Made in America”, the final scene.

hard_spoilers.reveal: Mad Men ends with Don Draper meditating on a clifftop retreat, smiling, and cutting straight to the 1971 Coca-Cola “Hilltop” ad — the implication being he went back and made it.
hard_spoilers.lands_because: The plot summary says he finds peace. The cut says he converted the peace into a commercial, which is the show's whole thesis about the man delivered in one edit. Whether that is redemption or damnation is the argument, and having a side in it means you were there.
hard_spoilers.where: Mad Men, “Person to Person”, the closing seconds.

content.premise: A run of hour-long American dramas, roughly 1999 onwards, made for cable and then for streaming, which asked to be taken as seriously as film. The Sopranos, The Wire, Mad Men, Breaking Bad and their descendants.
content.ending_summary: The endings are the argument. The Sopranos cuts to black mid-scene; Mad Men ends on an advertisement; Breaking Bad gives everyone what they asked for. Whether an ending earned itself is the conversation, not what happened in it.

characters.name: Tony Soprano
characters.role: The template for the difficult man at the centre of the genre.
characters.fate: Ambiguous, deliberately, and arguing about it is a rite of passage.

characters.name: Don Draper
characters.role: The other template: a man who is somebody else and knows it.
characters.fate: Ends on a hilltop, then on an advert.

major_events.title: The cut to black
major_events.description: The Sopranos finale ends mid-sentence. The reaction to it did as much for the genre's reputation as the show.

where_it_dips: Almost every one of these shows has a weak middle season, and saying which is proof you watched it.
The final season of a show renewed past its plan is the usual culprit.
Anything written around a contract dispute shows it.
